variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are defined using =: (global assignment) or =. (local assignment within explicit verbs).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
int =: 42
float =: 3.14
char =: 'a'
str =: 'hello'
bool =: 1  NB. Booleans are 0 and 1
complex =: 1j2
data_types.notes: J uses standard numeric, boolean, and character types. Data types are implicit based on values.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
sum =: 3 + 4
diff =: 10 - 5
prod =: 2 * 3
quot =: 10 % 2  NB. % is division
pow =: 2 ^ 3

eq =: 1 = 1
neq =: 1 ~: 2
gt =: 2 > 1
operators.notes: J restricts itself to the ASCII character set. Operators are called 'verbs'. Most standard symbols are reassigned (e.g., % is divide).

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
check =: 3 : 0
  if. y > 0 do.
    'Positive'
  else.
    'Non-positive'
  end.
)

NB. Array-oriented approach (agenda)
res =: ('Non-positive'`'Positive' @. (0&<)) 10
conditionals.notes: Explicit control structures (if. do. else. end.) require an explicit verb block. Agenda (@.) is often used for point-free conditionals.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
NB. Array-oriented implicit loop
squares =: *: i.5

NB. Explicit loop in a verb block
explicit_loop =: 3 : 0
  for_i. i.5 do.
    smoutput i
  end.
)
for_loop.notes: J prefers implicit operations over entire arrays. Explicit loops like for_i. operate sequentially but are much slower.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
loop_test =: 3 : 0
  x =. 0
  while. x < 5 do.
    smoutput x
    x =. x + 1
  end.
)
while_loop.notes: while. do. end. constructs a standard while loop inside explicit verb definitions.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
NB. Explicit verb
add =: 3 : 'y + 4'
res1 =: add 10

NB. Explicit dyadic verb (x and y arguments)
add_two =: 4 : 'x + y'
res2 =: 3 add_two 4

NB. Tacit verb
tacit_add =: +
functions.notes: Functions are called 'verbs'. y is the right argument, x is the left. Tacit programming eliminates explicit arguments entirely.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
vec =: 1 2 3 4 5
mat =: 2 3 $ 1 2 3 4 5 6  NB. Shape operator is $
shape =: $ mat

boxes =: (1 2 3);'abc'  NB. Heterogeneous data requires boxing (;)
arrays.notes: Arrays are built-in primitives. Shape ($) reshapes lists. Boxing (;) allows nested and mixed-type arrays.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
keys =: 'a';'b';'c'
vals =: 1;2;3

NB. Look up 'b'
idx =: keys i. <'b'
val =: idx { vals
maps.notes: J doesn't have a built-in map primitive, but boxed parallel arrays with the index of (i.) verb easily replicate dictionaries.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
safe_div =: 3 : 0
  try.
    10 % y
  catch.
    'Error occurred'
  end.
)
error_handling.notes: try. catch. end. allows trapping exceptions inside explicit verbs.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in J
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: J uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: J is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: J provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: J converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: J treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: J formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: J executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: J indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: J emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in J
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: J uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: J stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: J uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: J provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: J loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
